# Cross-asset hierarchical transfer at five-minute horizon — facts

> Source-anchored units about Cross-asset hierarchical transfer at five-minute horizon: 17 across 3 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

## Structure and components

- [statement] Research proposal, not an observed result: test a shared representation with a SOL-specific component against both full pooling and SOL-only estimation. Pindza supplies a simple hierarchical baseline and evidence of asset heterogeneity; Fused Encoder Networks supplies an example that retains a separate target encoder. Neither source validates this proposed combination for five-minute SOL perpetuals. (medium confidence) — https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/blockchain/articles/10.3389/fbloc.2026.1811716/full · keywords: Cross-asset hierarchical transfer at five-minute horizon · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2208.09968v3
- [statement] Pindza’s transfer finding is bounded by bar-derived microstructure proxies, a short historical window and one exchange. The author explicitly says the results may not generalise to other exchanges and that cross-exchange arbitrage dynamics are absent; this prevents treating the transfer matrix as universal market structure. (low confidence) — https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/blockchain/articles/10.3389/fbloc.2026.1811716/full · keywords: Cross-asset hierarchical transfer at five-minute horizon

## How it works

- [statement] Pindza’s hierarchical linear model pools feature effects across assets and uses an asset random intercept; it estimates on a random subsample for tractability. This is partial pooling of baseline returns, not evidence that every asset shares an identical predictive mechanism. (low confidence) — https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/blockchain/articles/10.3389/fbloc.2026.1811716/full · keywords: Cross-asset hierarchical transfer at five-minute horizon

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] In Pindza’s five-minute forward-return experiment, which includes Solana, models trained on one cryptocurrency fail to transfer to other cryptocurrencies. Treat this as a result for this dataset and model pipeline, not an impossibility theorem. (low confidence) — https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/blockchain/articles/10.3389/fbloc.2026.1811716/full · keywords: Cross-asset hierarchical transfer at five-minute horizon

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Verbii and colleagues study source selection for five-day cryptocurrency volatility. Their finding that marginal distribution similarity need not select the best source is a useful hypothesis for source selection, but the forecast target and horizon differ from five-minute SOL returns. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35314 · keywords: Cross-asset hierarchical transfer at five-minute horizon
- [statement] Poh and colleagues propose Fused Encoder Networks with separate source and target modules and report favorable cryptocurrency momentum results. This is evidence that transfer can work in another financial task, rather than confirmation of five-minute SOL microstructure transfer. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.09968 · keywords: Cross-asset hierarchical transfer at five-minute horizon
- [statement] In Pindza’s zero-shot LightGBM transfer experiment, transfer correlations are lower across cryptocurrencies than between the same cryptocurrency’s spot and futures markets. Treat this as evidence against assuming universal five-minute microstructure transfer, rather than a theorem excluding all transfer methods. (low confidence) — https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/blockchain/articles/10.3389/fbloc.2026.1811716/full · keywords: Cross-asset hierarchical transfer at five-minute horizon
- [statement] Poh, Roberts and Zohren provide a concrete transfer architecture: Fused Encoder Networks run a pretrained source encoder alongside a target encoder and concatenate their outputs. Their empirical use-case is weekly crypto momentum with foreign-exchange source data, so the architecture is a candidate mechanism rather than direct five-minute SOL evidence. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2208.09968v3 · keywords: Cross-asset hierarchical transfer at five-minute horizon

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Pindza’s MAML exercise uses a linear base learner with one task-specific gradient step. The author describes it as a feature-importance and robustness check, so its presence does not demonstrate a profitable adapted SOL trading strategy. (low confidence) — https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/blockchain/articles/10.3389/fbloc.2026.1811716/full · keywords: Cross-asset hierarchical transfer at five-minute horizon
- [statement] Bieganowski and Ślepaczuk report similar feature importance and SHAP shapes across cryptocurrencies. Their prediction target is a three-second mid-price return; this supports investigating reusable features, but does not establish five-minute cross-asset weight transfer. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2602.00776v1 · keywords: Cross-asset hierarchical transfer at five-minute horizon
- [statement] Wang and colleagues describe negative transfer as a less related source hurting target performance and propose filtering unrelated source data. This provides a general methodological reason to test target-only baselines; it is not crypto-specific validation. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.09751 · keywords: Cross-asset hierarchical transfer at five-minute horizon
- [statement] The Janus README describes five-minute multi-asset pretraining followed by thirty-minute supervised fine-tuning. That documented pipeline is an implementation lead, not validation of a five-minute SOL deployment. (low confidence) — https://github.com/aurumco/janus · keywords: Cross-asset hierarchical transfer at five-minute horizon
- [statement] The arXiv record marks Hierarchical Projection for Adaptive Knowledge Transfer as withdrawn and states that a proof mistake needs revision. Exclude it as affirmative evidence that hierarchical transfer works. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-06-28) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.08691 · keywords: Cross-asset hierarchical transfer at five-minute horizon
- [statement] Pindza studies the five-minute forward log return using minute-level Binance spot and perpetual-futures data for six cryptocurrencies, including Solana, over August 2025–February 2026. This is direct horizon evidence, restricted to that historical sample. (low confidence) — https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/blockchain/articles/10.3389/fbloc.2026.1811716/full · keywords: Cross-asset hierarchical transfer at five-minute horizon
- [statement] The Fused Encoder Networks paper reports stronger crypto momentum performance than its benchmarks, but its weekly rebalancing and weekly data prevent interpreting that result as demonstrated five-minute transfer. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2208.09968v3 · keywords: Cross-asset hierarchical transfer at five-minute horizon
- [statement] Verbii, Killinkarov and Yafarov report that distant-source selection can outperform nearest-source selection for some learner families, and that forward pilot selection improves on random transfer. Their task is five-day crypto volatility; they explicitly restrict the findings to an exploratory historical panel. This scopes any claim that marginal source similarity alone determines useful transfer. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35314v1 · keywords: Cross-asset hierarchical transfer at five-minute horizon
- [statement] Methodological inference for the SOL experiment: compare transferred or pooled models against a SOL-only model under the same chronological test boundaries, and select source assets using earlier target validation data. Pindza’s weak cross-asset results and Verbii et al.’s target-only, self-continuation and forward-pilot controls motivate this comparison; they do not establish its SOL performance. (medium confidence) — https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/blockchain/articles/10.3389/fbloc.2026.1811716/full · keywords: Cross-asset hierarchical transfer at five-minute horizon · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35314v1
